title: econ-sweeper: workload-aware microbatch shaping + KV-cache pruning with unit-econ safety net
author: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce 'econ-sweeper', a runtime component that adjusts microbatch sizing and performs conservative KV-cache pruning driven by a unit-economics signal. Motivation: many workloads have bimodal sequence-length distributions and transient cache pressure; static batching + LRU-only cache policies either blow cost targets or cause tail latency spikes. This change implements a lightweight controller that observes per-route token cost, 95th-latency, and cold-cache miss patterns and applies two coordinated levers: (1) shape_tuner: nudges target microbatch size and microscopic batching window to match observed latency/cost SLOs; (2) cache_sweeper: age-based and value-importance-aware pruning for model KV caches (early pruning of rarely-hit prefixes plus hot-key pinning). Key properties: - workload-driven but conservative by default: the controller starts in read-only sampling mode and proposes changes; after a safe confidence window changes are applied incrementally. - Safety nets: immediate rollback on SLO regressions (configured via route-level policy), and a per-deployment kill-switch. - Integrations with Redwood Optimize: recommendations surfaced to console and can be applied automatically by teams who opt-in. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4521) - [x] unit tests for controller logic - [x] integration tests in perf-canary harness - [x] feature flag (econ_sweeper.enabled) - [x] observability: metrics + tracing + rollout events - [x] docs and console surface for recommendations Migration notes: Feature is behind a flag off by default. Enabling on a route will create new debug metrics (econ_sweeper.proposals, econ_sweeper.applied_changes, econ_sweeper.rollback_events). See README.md in runtime/batcher for opt-in instructions. Example runtime config snippet: {"route": "/chat", "econ_sweeper": {"mode": "auto", "max_latency_p99_increase_pct": 5, "min_cost_reduction_target_pct": 7, "confidence_window": 600000}}

review_comments: Ben Crawford: Nice direction. A few questions about stability - how do you avoid oscillation when traffic patterns change frequently?
Aisha Patel: We apply a backoff and hysteresis window; proposals are only acted on after the configured confidence_window and require monotonic improvement in the unit-econ metric.
Marta Gomez: Can we get a mode that only simulates (no actual pruning) and emits dry-run reports?
Aisha Patel: Yes - added 'mode': "dry_run" in config; console will show proposals but won't apply them.
Chris Nguyen: CI showed a flaky test on cache eviction in Windows build, reran and passed on second run.
Samir Rao (approver): Approving after address of one nit (move telemetry keys under econ_sweeper.* namespace).
release_notes: Adds experimental econ_sweeper controller to dynamically tune microbatch sizing and perform conservative KV-cache pruning. Off by default; opt-in via runtime config. Exposes new metrics and console recommendations. Safe rollback on SLO regressions.
